_about: Chapter 3's boss: the ghost of level 3-32 (level31b), decoded from android_game.bin,
ETHCallback_ghost (bytes 451999..457261) with its helpers in the same file.
It is the game's SECOND boss and shares nothing with the first. The beholder glides,
throws rolling stones, is hurt by a stone rising through it, fires rings of spikes and
raises a button when it dies. The ghost flies a waypoint path, shoots the player, is hurt
by FIRE, summons a minion when hurt, and drops a KEY when it dies. Boss.hpp is the
beholder's and stays that way; this is its own module for that reason.
FIVE states, not four, and their numbers are written into the callback's first six
instructions: APPEARING 0, SHOOTING 1, RAGE_MODE 2, DAMAGE 3, DEATH 4, and
GHOST_RADIUS 64. The init block writes hp 3, elapsedTime 0, state 0 and shotsFired 0.
HOW IT IS HURT, which is the whole reason this step follows the fire diamond. The
SHOOTING arm ends with isBurned(this): burned, it goes to DAMAGE, takes hp += -1, calls
healBurn(this) and plays playGhostDamageSound. Nothing else in the level can burn it, so
the fire diamond IS the weapon - the fireballs a converted portal shot becomes. A port
that built this boss without the fire diamond would have an invulnerable boss.
WHAT LEVEL31B IS. The level holds a keyhole (152, 204) and a door_locked (120, 160),
both metadata/color yellow, and NO KEY ANYWHERE. The only key in the level is the one
this boss drops when it dies. So the fight is the lock, and Keys is what opens it.

_note: The boss_spawn node, and it is NOT shaped like the beholder's. An adder carries
metadata/entity naming what to spawn ('beholder.ent'), and Boss::Plays reads that
field. ghost_pos carries no `entity` metadata at all - the NODE NAME is the whole of
it - so Ghost::Plays matches the entity name instead. Mirroring Boss::Plays literally
would return false for every level and leave level31b inert with no visible cause.
entity_roles.json files all four bosses under boss_spawn: adder (1-32), dragon.ent
(2-32), ghost_pos (3-32), dark_dragon_spawn (4-32) and dragon_knight_spawn. The role is
deliberately NOT in Roles::IsPorted; test_mp_start asks per NODE instead, so building
one boss never claims another. level31a's dragon stays inert and stays honest.
The APPEARING arm flies a WaypointManager rather than gliding. Four waypoints are
added in the init block; Waypoint's constructor is (pos, time, color, filter, angle),
read off Waypoint::Waypoint's parameters, and getCurrentPoint interpolates pos, color
and angle between the current waypoint and the next with the CURRENT one's filter
applied to the timer's bias. The angle is used as a uniform SetScale and the colour's
alpha as SetAlpha, so the ghost fades and swells into being.
mid_fraction is the quarter in midPoint = currentPos + (ghost_pos - currentPos) / 4.
_seeds_note: On WaypointManager::isLastFrame the arm sets state SHOOTING, shotsFired 0 and
elapsedTime 3000 - NOT zero. Seeding the clock at the shot interval means the first
shot comes on the first frame of SHOOTING rather than three seconds later.

_note: Every interval it seeks dark_mage.ent - the PLAYER - and fires only when the player's
x is past the x of the level's red_line entity. level31b puts red_line at (262, 110),
so the boss does not shoot at a player still on the left of the arena.
It also restocks the player's tools on that same beat, with addEntityIfItCantBeFound:
a barrel_bomb at barrel_spawn and a fire_diamond.ent at fire_diamond_spawn. That is
why level31b places both spawn markers, and why dropping the fire diamond down the
gutter mouth is survivable - the boss hands you another.
addEnemyShoot and ETHCallback_enemy_shoot are in ETHCallback_minion.angelscript, and
minions.json's _shooting_not_built already decoded them: enemy_shoot.ent carries
direction, destiny, casterPos, targetName and targetID, moves 120 units a second, and
kills with fakeRadius = scale(16) - an isCharacter target within that has hp set to 0.
killPortal is NOT reachable from this boss. That branch fires only when the shot's
target is named portal.ent, and the ghost always passes the player as its target. So
the step minions.json deferred stays deferred, and this shot only kills the player.
The muzzle flash (projectile_shoot.ent) and the portal_mark.ent that telegraphs where
the shot will land are presentation and are not built.
hp <= 0 goes straight to DEATH. Otherwise it holds at alpha 0.5, bounces, scatters
explosions, and after 4000 ms goes to RAGE_MODE rather than back to SHOOTING.
RAGE_MODE waits on its escort. While no minion.ent exists it spawns one - inside the
first 200 ms of the state - at the position of the level's minion_spawn_point, on the
wayA prefix, via spawnMinion. Once one exists it STAYS in rage until that minion is
gone; then the 200 ms window has passed and it returns to SHOOTING at alpha 1.
minion_spawn_point is NOT a minion_spawn marker and carries no role at all, which is
why Minions::Find never sees it and why this module resolves it by name. level31b puts
it at (436, 96); the wayA prefix resolves wayA0 (314, 208) hold 1000 and wayA1
(412, 208) hold 4000, which minions.json calls 'unclaimed' and assigns to this boss.
DEATH stops the boss music, bounces at 1.25 over 400 ms, scatters explosions, and at
3550 ms calls explode(pos, 2.0, 0), adds key.ent at its own position and deletes
itself.
The key's colour is NOT taken from level31b. key.ent's own CustomData holds exactly one
variable - a string named color with the value yellow - so every key.ent the game ever
adds is yellow by the entity's default, and level31b's keyhole and door being yellow is
the level agreeing with the entity rather than the source of the value.
blast_scale is recorded and NOT applied: explode's own radius is fire.json's blast_px,
and what the 2.0 multiplies is not established. The port drops the key and does not
blast, which is the conservative reading - a blast that killed the player at the moment
of victory would be a worse error than a missing one.

_not_built: DAMAGE and DEATH both scatter small_explosion_no_light.ent through overTimeEntityAdder
at 400 ms, at an offset of scale(64) * (0.4 + randF(0.7)) along a random angle, built
as (-cos, sin). Presentation in a renderer-free port, and random - recorded, not built.
The picture and the noise: ghost_appear_effect.ent, the frame changes (0 in SHOOTING,
3 in RAGE_MODE), the alpha and scale the waypoints drive, the bounces, the explosions,
playGameMusic and the boss music the DEATH arm stops, and all five ghost sounds.
The ghost_minion. level31b's minion_spawn carries metadata/entityName ghost_minion.ent -
the ONLY use of that field in all 128 levels - and ETHCallback_ghost_minion tints itself
black, delegates wholesale to ETHCallback_minion, and on death spawns a ghost.ent and
deletes itself. The port spawns the default minion there, as minions.json records, so
that transformation does not happen. It costs nothing playable: the spawned ghost.ent is
not this boss and has no callback of its own that any level reads.
The barrel bomb restock. addEntityIfItCantBeFound would put a barrel_bomb at
barrel_spawn; Fire owns bombs and fills them from the scene, so a mid-run bomb is the
same mid-run-Add step minions.json names for Fire::Burnable and Demolish::Breakable.
The FIRE DIAMOND restock IS built, because Diamonds holds its diamonds in a plain
vector and a diamond is not a body.
